note: depth pass 1: L4 例词补充

words.glossEn: deliberately mysterious; hidden in meaning
words.etymology: 希腊 kryptos「隐藏的」+ -ic；同族 crypt（地窖）、cryptography
derivation: crypt（隐藏）+ -ic（形容词后缀）→ cryptic
words.example: His answer was so cryptic that nobody understood it.

words.glossEn: a message written in cipher
words.etymology: crypt（隐藏）+ -o-（连接元音）+ -gram（写下的东西）
derivation: crypt + o + gram → cryptogram
words.example: The agent hid a cryptogram inside the advertisement.

words.glossEn: consisting of two parts or having two functions
words.etymology: 拉丁 dualis < duo「二」，与 duet、duplicate 同族
derivation: du（二）+ -al → dual
words.example: The aircraft uses a dual control system.

words.glossEn: to make an exact copy of something
words.etymology: 拉丁 duplicare < du-（二）+ plicare（折叠）
derivation: du（二）+ plic（折叠）+ -ate → 折成两层 → 复制
words.example: Please duplicate this file before you edit it.

words.glossEn: the fortified upper part of an ancient Greek city
words.etymology: 希腊 akros「最高的、尖端的」+ polis「城邦」
derivation: acr（高处）+ o + pol（城）+ -is → 高处的城
words.example: The Acropolis of Athens stands on a limestone hill.

words.glossEn: a word formed from the initial letters of other words
words.etymology: 希腊 akron「末端、开头」+ onyma「名字」
derivation: acr（尖端、开头）+ onym（名字）→ 取首字母成词
words.example: NASA is an acronym for a long agency name.

words.glossEn: the practice of farming land and raising crops
words.etymology: 拉丁 ager/agri「田地」+ cultura「耕作」
derivation: agr（田地）+ i + cult（耕种）+ -ure → 耕种田地
words.example: Agriculture still employs half the region's workers.

words.glossEn: the science of crop production and soil management
words.etymology: 希腊 agros「田地」+ nomos「管理、法则」
derivation: agr（田地）+ o + -nomy（管理法则）→ 田地管理的学问
words.example: She took a degree in agronomy before returning to the farm.

words.glossEn: to give life, spirit, or motion to
words.etymology: 拉丁 anima「气息、灵魂」+ -ate
derivation: anim（灵魂、生命）+ -ate（动词后缀）→ 注入生命
words.example: A skilled teacher can animate a dull textbook chapter.

words.glossEn: a living creature that is not a plant
words.etymology: 拉丁 animalis < anima「气息、生命」
derivation: anim（生命、气息）+ -al → 有气息者
words.example: The fox is a nocturnal animal.

words.glossEn: a vehicle that carries sick or injured people
words.etymology: 拉丁 ambulare「走动」+ -ance；原指野战移动医院
derivation: ambul（走动）+ -ance → 可移动的救护设施
words.example: An ambulance reached the scene in four minutes.

words.glossEn: able to walk; relating to walking
words.etymology: 拉丁 ambulatorius < ambulare「走动」
derivation: ambul（走）+ -at- + -ory → 与行走有关的
words.example: The patient was ambulatory on the second day after surgery.

words.glossEn: the yearly return of a date worth remembering
words.etymology: 拉丁 anniversarius < annus「年」+ vertere「转」
derivation: ann（年）+ i + vers（转）+ -ary → 每年转回的那一天
words.example: They marked their tenth anniversary with a quiet dinner.

words.glossEn: lasting through the year or recurring year after year
words.etymology: 拉丁 perennis < per-（贯穿）+ annus/ennus「年」
derivation: per（贯穿）+ enn（年）+ -ial → 贯穿全年
words.example: Traffic congestion is a perennial complaint in the city.

words.glossEn: the study of human societies and cultures
words.etymology: 希腊 anthropos「人」+ -logia「学问」
derivation: anthrop（人）+ o + logy（学科）→ 研究人的学问
words.example: He switched from law to anthropology in his second year.

words.glossEn: the giving of money or help for human welfare
words.etymology: 希腊 philanthrōpia < philein「爱」+ anthropos「人」
derivation: phil（爱）+ anthrop（人）+ -y → 爱人之举
words.example: Her philanthropy paid for three rural schools.

words.glossEn: loud enough to be heard
words.etymology: 拉丁 audire「听」+ -ibilis「能够」
derivation: aud（听）+ -ible（能…的）→ 能听到的
words.example: The warning tone was barely audible over the engines.

words.glossEn: the people who watch or listen to a performance
words.etymology: 拉丁 audientia < audire「听」
derivation: aud（听）+ i + -ence → 听的人
words.example: The audience stayed for the whole question session.

words.glossEn: relating to the ear or to hearing
words.etymology: 拉丁 auris「耳」+ -al
derivation: aur（耳）+ -al → 耳的
words.example: The test measures both visual and aural memory.

words.glossEn: the visible outer part of the ear
words.etymology: 拉丁 auricula「小耳」，auris「耳」的指小形式
derivation: aur（耳）+ -icle（指小）→ 小耳 → 耳廓
words.example: The surgeon repaired a small tear in the auricle.
